same_task_reread_share.source: measure.js.txt over rows.jsonl (rows written by loc.js.txt; writer levels as in own.js.txt)
same_task_reread_share.definition: a call re-reads its own task working file when the same agent transcript wrote it (strict), or the same session (orchestrator plus its subagents) wrote it under 24 hours before (task). "Same session any age" is the loose upper bound; one session ran 310 hours.

premise_kind_shares.source: measure.js.txt over classify2.json (hand classification; classify2.js.txt splits kind c)
premise_kind_shares.unit: share of the 60 sampled findings that have at least one premise of the kind

a.definition: fact computable from this repository at a commit by a fixed query

ax.definition: fact computable from the other (clinic) repository at a commit

b.definition: span of a file tracked in this repository

bx.definition: span of a file tracked in the other repository

c_repo.definition: span of a file in this repository folder, not tracked

c_scratch.definition: span of a scratch file or transcript outside the repository

c_other.definition: span of an untracked file in the other repository

d.definition: measurement run once, inputs not kept

e.definition: outside source (paper, web page, video, tool docs)

epin.definition: third-party library source at a version pinned by a tracked lockfile

f.definition: agent judgement with no checkable premise

premise_counts.note: premise-level shares are clustered within findings; use the finding-level shares for inference

definitions.tracked: premise kinds a or b: recoverable from git at a commit of this repository
definitions.folder: tracked, or c_repo: a file that sits in the repository folder but is not committed (can change or vanish with no record)

headline_tracked_checkable.definition: every checkable premise is tracked in this repository (a, b); agent judgement (f) may sit on top

tracked_strict.definition: every premise is a or b, and no premise is bare agent judgement

folder_checkable.definition: every checkable premise is in the repository folder, tracked or not (a, b, c_repo); f may sit on top

any_version_control_or_pinned_checkable.definition: every checkable premise is in some version control or pinned (a, b, ax, bx, epin); f may sit on top

counterfactual_every_cited_file_content_.definition: if every cited file (any place) had been content-hashed when cited: every checkable premise is a file span or a repository query, none a one-off measurement or outside source; f may sit on top

has_any_tracked_premise.definition: at least one premise a or b

has_premise_outside_repository_folder.definition: at least one premise outside this repository folder (other repo, scratch, one-off measurement, outside source)

has_unrecheckable_premise.definition: at least one premise that cannot be re-checked at all (d or f)

only_judgement_or_none.definition: no checkable premise at all (judgement only)

deterministic_finding_share.source: measure.js.txt over classify2.json (finding type and r9 fields)

type_Q_query_and_answer.definition: finding is a deterministic query plus its answer (type Q)

type_Q_recheckable_now_in_repo.definition: type Q and every checkable premise tracked in this repository

type_M_one_off_script_result.definition: finding is the result of a script run (deterministic in form, but inputs mostly unkept)

expressible_as_query.definition: expressible as a query if its inputs had been kept: finding type Q (query and answer) or M (one-off script result)

interpretation.definition: interpretation that only a model or a person can re-check

headline.acted_on: not established: the scan cannot tell whether a decision rested on the stale sentence

could_not_measure: Whether a stale finding was acted on: the scan finds where the sentence was shown again and what the transcript wrote next, not whether a decision rested on it; judging that needs a reading of the transcripts, which this lane did not do.

Staleness of findings whose premises are outside git (scratch files, untracked evidence, the other repository, outside sources, one-off measurements): there is no history to compare against; only 8 findings with repository premises were traced, 3 of them changed.
Use as opposed to exposure: a finding shown in a tool result was not necessarily read or used (9 % of model calls carry visible text, use-cases.md 2.3).
Four sampled findings (C4, G2, I4, J4) were not found in any transcript: their needle crosses a line break in the source file.
The CQ1 label is the noisiest of use-cases.md: it is a heuristic label on reads of notes, reports and verdict files, not a judged intent.
Premise counts are one coder's hand judgement (first pass 2026-11-13, kind c split 2026-11-14), with no second coder and no agreement figure.
The 12 source files were chosen by hand among files with high CQ1 reads, sessions or carried tokens that hold findings; the ranks are in findings-classified.json, the choice itself is not random.
Commit state of untracked files at the time a finding was written: untracked files have no history; c_repo is judged by where a copy sits now.
The window after the two stale changes is 5.4 hours (the transcript corpus ends 2026-11-13 15:24 UTC), so the stale-use count covers almost no time.
Web: no CQ1 call was a web fetch (web share 0); outside sources enter only as premises cited inside notes.
